title: Signal Catcher: weekly applied-ml notes (quant + eval + onboarding)
body:
Date: 2026-11-10
Owners: Priya (notes), Marco (experiments), Elena (eval harness)
Attendees: Priya, Marco, Elena, Jasper, Anya (SRE drop-in)

Purpose: quick sync to capture signals (regressions, flaky experiments, onboarding blockers) rather than polished retrospective. Use as single source for devs doing fast follow-ups.

Top-line summary:
- Ran a focused smoke-suite for Llama-3-7B-int8 (dynamic quant) across our standard eval set + a tiny code-gen slice. Observed latency improvement ~2.6x on p3d. But token-level perplexity is stable while code-gen accuracy (unit test pass@1) dropped by ~8pp on 50-sample subset.
- KV-cache eviction experiment surfaced a bug in our continuous-batching path where an eviction during stream flush can nuke the active request (race). SRE suggested a tight mutex around cache->flush; we need a less blocking approach.
- Model onboarding checklist for external community variant (alpaca-7b-finetune) needs extra metadata: tokenizer provenance, sample rate for position embeddings, and a mapping for model_variant->quant_profile. Without that mapping, runtime picks default fp16 and we blow memory.

Notes / observations (raw):
- Marco: ran 5 seeds of quantize-dyn (per-layer symmetric) -> int8. Latency numbers (median tail):
    * fp16 baseline: 210ms median / 340ms p95 (bs=1, seq=512)
    * int8 dyn: 78ms median / 120ms p95 -> ~2.7x median speedup but p95 variability higher for long context (seq>1024).
- Memory: int8 reduces active model memory by 48% but intermediate activations still dominate; need activation checkpointing + tuned batch sizing in serving.
- Eval: Elena reports coarse eval suite shows comparable language modeling loss, but the code-gen micro-suite (50 curated tasks) shows pass@1 drop from 42% -> 34% after quant. Hypothesis: quant noise interacting with layernorm scaling for certain instruction prefixes. Action: run weight-sensitivity mapping (per-layer KL).
- KV-cache bug: repro steps in GH-rl/serve#342. Short version: continuous-batching path merges requests, then cache eviction triggered by background cleaner removes a slice while a streamer tries to write tokens; streamer gets nil KV slice -> panics recovered but request returns empty chunk.
    * Immediate mitigation: add CAS flag on cache entries for in-flight tokens (low-risk stopgap).
    * Long term: consider reference-counted cache segments or epoch-based cache invalidation to avoid per-request locks.
- Onboarding: Jasper found we accept model.tar.gz with a minimal manifest but not the tokenizer.json metadata we rely on for byte-pair merges. For community models we should fail fast with a clear message.

Decisions made:
- Roll back the int8 variant from the hosted smoke ring while we investigate code-gen regressions. Keep a canary in dedicated infra where we can trace and reproduce. (assigned: Marco, due: 2026-11-12)
- Patch the KV-cache with a CAS guard as immediate fix and schedule design review for cache re-architecture. (assigned: Priya + SRE, due: 2026-11-16)
- Add two onboarding guardrails to the importer pipeline: explicit tokenizer metadata required, and model_manifest must include quant_profile tag (enum: none | int8-dyn | int8-static | q4f32). If missing, import flags "requires-manual-review". (assigned: Jasper, due: 2026-11-17)

Action items (short):
- Marco: weight-sensitivity runs + per-layer KL report for Llama-3-7B-int8 (small corpus) -- JIRA-1284 -- due 2026-11-13.
- Elena: extend code-gen eval suite to 300 examples and run full sweep across seeds for int8 vs fp16; include failure traces and prompt prefixes. (linked GH perf harness). due 2026-11-15.
- Priya: implement CAS guard on kv-cache and push hotfix branch for smoke tests. Add regression test that simulates eviction during streaming. due 2026-11-12.
- Jasper: onboarding manifest change + importer validation messages + docs PR. due 2026-11-17.
- SRE (Anya): run load test of patched kv-cache on dedicated cluster to validate throughput impact of CAS. due 2026-11-18.

Open questions / discussion backlog:
- Is the code-gen regression specific to certain instruction templates? Early signal says yes (chain-of-thought-like prompts more affected). We need deeper prompt slicing.
- Should quant profiles be part of canned rollouts so we can auto-fallback to fp16 on quality regression? We have tooling in Optimize for model policies but not for per-variant rollouts. Proposal: add model_variant policies to rollout config.
- Cache re-architecture: do we prefer epoch invalidation (cheap, coarse) or reference-counted segments (more complex but precise)? Schedule design session.

Quick experiment log (raw numbers):
- experiment: llama-3-7b int8-dyn on p3d (5 runs, bs1, seq512)
    run1: median=80ms p95=125ms loss=2.11 code-pass@1=36%
    run2: median=76ms p95=118ms loss=2.09 code-pass@1=34%
    run3: median=82ms p95=128ms loss=2.10 code-pass@1=35%
    baseline fp16 (same hardware): median=210ms p95=340ms loss=2.07 code-pass@1=42%

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep these logs terse; they get noisy. Add a small tag prefix like [SMOKE] or [REGRESSION] to make searching easier.
- When filing follow-ups, link to this doc and prefix JIRA with "quant-signal/" for quick filtering.

Meeting wrap: next sync Tue 2026-11-16 09:30 PT (30m). Agenda: review Marco's per-layer KL heatmap, Elena's expanded eval, SRE load test results.

Raw links (copy-paste):
- GH bug + repro: https://github.com/redwood-rl/serve/pull/342
- JIRA ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/JIRA-1284
